answer: Synchronized memory-hard proof-of-work resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to solve a key-bound Argon2id puzzle after a randomness beacon drops and submit the proof before a tight cutoff. Because DRAM-bandwidth saturation stops one host from solving concurrent puzzles, attackers must lease dedicated memory and power per identity. However, strict deadlines exclude energy-starved edge units like solar sensors in a grove coated in umber dust or relays on an icy summit.
